nodes.title: Flatness of a sheaf over the parameter base
nodes.statement: For f:X→S and a quasi-coherent O_X-module F, IsFlatOver(f,F) means that for every affine open U⊆S and affine open V⊆f⁻¹(U), Γ(V,F) is flat over Γ(U,O_S), with scalar restriction along f#_{U,V}. This is equivalent to flatness of F_x over O_{S,f(x)} at every x. It is a property of the sheaf relative to f, not flatness of f itself.
hypotheses: X and S arbitrary schemes; F quasi-coherent; no finite-presentation or Noetherian assumption.
proofSteps: Use the existing sheaf of modules and its sections, restricting scalars along the existing scheme map on affine sections.
Localization of flat modules proves the stalk criterion and its converse on affine covers.
Tensor-product pullback preserves relative flatness under every cartesian base change; an isomorphism of sheaves preserves it.

nodes.title: A fixed-polynomial flat quotient family
nodes.statement: For separated finitely presented f:X→S, a finitely presented quasi-coherent E, an f-relatively very ample invertible sheaf L and P∈Q[t], a QuotFamily over T→S consists of a surjection q:E_T→F of O_{X_T}-modules, with F finitely presented and T-flat, support proper over T, and χ(X_t,F_t⊗L_t^n)=P(n) for every t and all sufficiently large n. Coherent on a locally Noetherian test scheme means finitely presented; for arbitrary T the finite-presentation condition is retained explicitly. No S-flatness of X or E is imposed.
hypotheses: L and P fixed; arbitrary test schemes T; use proper support, not merely closed support.
In the projective case proper support follows from projectivity of X_T→T.
proofSteps: Use the native sheaf pullback to form E_T and L_T; finite presentation and quasi-coherence are supplier/base-library conditions.
Use the support supplied by SF.0/coherent-scheme-support and the relative-flatness predicate.
Use R09.1 fibre Hilbert polynomials, with Euler characteristics only under finite-dimensionality and eventual higher-cohomology vanishing.

sources.match: Families retain the surjection, finite presentation, flatness, proper support and fibre polynomial. The projectivity theorem allows a coherent source sheaf without a flatness hypothesis.

nodes.title: Quotient equivalence is equality of kernels
nodes.statement: For two epimorphisms q:E_T→F and q′:E_T→F′, equivalence means an O_{X_T}-module isomorphism a:F≅F′ with q followed by a=q′. Such an a, if it exists, is unique. It exists if and only if the kernel subobjects in E_T are equal. Pullback preserves this equivalence even when E_T is not T-flat; it does not identify inequivalent maps merely because F and F′ are isomorphic.
hypotheses: The quotient maps are epimorphisms in the native abelian category of sheaves of modules.
proofSteps: Both epimorphisms are cokernels of their kernels in the native abelian category.
Equal kernels give the unique induced cokernel isomorphism; cancellation by an epimorphism proves uniqueness.
Right exactness transports the commuting isomorphism under pullback.

sources.match: The functor identifies quotients by isomorphisms commuting with their source maps, equivalently by their kernels.

nodes.title: The fixed-polynomial Quot functor
nodes.statement: Quot^P_{E/X/S}:(Sch/S)^op→Sets sends T→S to QuotFamily(X_T→T,E_T,L_T,P) modulo the unique source-commuting isomorphisms. Pullback gives the maps. This is an fpqc sheaf and preserves filtered affine limits when f is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and finitely presented and E is finitely presented. Its fixed-polynomial condition is open and closed in the unbounded Quot functor in the projective setting.
hypotheses: f separated and finitely presented; E finitely presented and quasi-coherent; L relatively very ample for polynomial assertions.
All test schemes are admitted, including nonreduced and non-Noetherian ones.
proofSteps: Pass to the quotient setoid from quotient-equivalence; right exact pullback defines its functor maps.
Import fpqc quasi-coherent descent from R09.3. Finite presentation, epimorphy, relative flatness and proper support descend; fibre polynomials descend after residue-field extension.

Import SF.0 finite-presentation limits, supplemented by the requested descent of relative flatness of a finitely presented module. Descend the quotient and its surjectivity at a finite stage; fibre polynomials are locally constant by R09.1.

nodes.title: The fixed-polynomial Hilbert functor
nodes.statement: Hilb^P_{X/S}(T) is the set of closed subschemes Z⊆X_T with Z→T flat, proper and finitely presented and fibre Hilbert polynomial P for L|Z. It retains the actual closed embedding, including its ideal and nilpotents. Pullback of ideal sheaves defines the functor on all test schemes.
hypotheses: X→S separated finitely presented; L relatively very ample for the polynomial.
Closed subschemes are native IdealSheafData, not subsets of points.
proofSteps: Use native ideal-sheaf closed subschemes and their arbitrary base change.
Use the finite-presentation/proper-support sheaf O_Z pushed along Z→X_T.
Flatness of O_Z over T is equivalent to flatness of Z→T; apply the structure-sheaf criterion.

sources.match: Hilbert families are flat proper finitely presented closed subschemes with the prescribed polynomial.
The definition uses closed subschemes on arbitrary test schemes and identifies their structure-sheaf quotients.

nodes.title: Flattening strata for a coherent projective sheaf
nodes.statement: For Noetherian S and coherent F on P^n_S, there is a finite set of numerical polynomials P and locally closed immersions S_P→S whose underlying sets partition S. For every T→S, F_T is T-flat with polynomial P exactly when T→S factors through S_P; the factor is unique. This is a universal scheme-theoretic flattening stratification, not a partition by ranks on points. The disjoint union need not be a closed subscheme or an open cover of S.
hypotheses: F need not be S-flat; all test schemes T are included using finite-presentation limits.
proofSteps: R09.1 eventual cohomology yields finite presentations of the finitely many needed twisted pushforwards. Their rank loci give candidate locally closed strata.
Impose the remaining higher-twist relations as ideals; Noetherian stabilization produces the final scheme structure. Polynomial values at n+1 sufficiently large integers fix the polynomial.

Use the cohomology/flatness criterion with higher-cohomology vanishing, not constant fibre dimensions over nonreduced bases; extend the locally Noetherian proof to every T by the requested module-limit descent.

sources.match: Locally closed polynomial strata universally detect flat pullbacks; their ideals encode more than the ranks of fibres.

nodes.title: Bounded Quot families in a Grassmannian
nodes.statement: Work over an affine Noetherian open of S with X↪P^n_S and a chosen O_X(-a)^p↠E. R09.1 gives m≫a, uniform for quotients with polynomial P, for which F(m) is generated and higher cohomology vanishes on every fibre. Then π_{T*}F(m) is locally free of rank P(m), commutes with every base change, and the quotient of the fixed finite free space H⁰(P^n,O(m-a))^p gives a point of the imported Grassmannian of rank-P(m) quotients. This transformation is injective. The evaluation of the Grassmannian kernel in E(m) reconstructs F(m) as a cokernel; flattening this universal cokernel gives its scheme-theoretic locally closed image. The numerical rank P(m) is asserted when a family over a nonempty test base exists. Polynomials with no such families are represented by the empty locus; the functor still has its unique point on the empty test base. The chosen evaluation map from the fixed section space to E(m) is retained in the construction data and used in reconstruction.
hypotheses: Noetherian affine base; specified projective embedding and finite presentation of E; m a uniform bound supplied by R09.1.
Use the image of the pulled evaluation relations, without pretending kernel pullback is exact when E is not flat.
proofSteps: Import R09.1/uniform-quotient-regularity and family-regularity. Choose a common bound for the finite set of fibre polynomials of the fixed ambient E, retaining the corrected extra step in the regularity index noted by the R09.1 review. If no geometric-fibre quotient has P, use the empty representing locus directly; otherwise P(m) is a nonnegative integer at the common bound.
Apply cohomology and base change under higher-cohomology vanishing; the uniform fibre regularity applies to every family over every test base.

Use ModularCurves 0G for the Grassmannian and its universal quotient; evaluation defines a universal cokernel. Its flattened P stratum represents exactly the original families. Retain the evaluation map determined by the projective presentation. Pull its relations to E(m), take their cokernel, and untwist by L^(-m); recovery identifies the source map as well as the target sheaf.
Closed equations impose that a quotient of the presenting free sheaf factors through E. These are vanishing loci of morphisms into a flat coherent target, from Nitsure Theorem 3.5.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.3, pp. 11–13; Theorem 3.5, pp. 16–17; proof of Theorem 5.1, pp. 25–28

acceptance: Increasing m beyond the bound yields the same Quot functor, not a new moduli object.

Negative or nonintegral constant polynomials have no quotient families over a nonempty test base; the empty test base still has one family. Do not force P(m) to be a natural number for every rational polynomial.

nodes.title: Projective representability of fixed Quot
nodes.statement: Let S be Noetherian, X→S projective, L relatively very ample and E coherent. For each P∈Q[t], Quot^P_{E/X/S} is represented on all test schemes by a projective finitely presented S-scheme. No flatness of X/S or E/S is required. Here projective means an immersion as a closed subscheme of a projective bundle P(V) for a coherent finite-presentation sheaf V; a global immersion into P^N_S or P(V) with V locally free is claimed only under the corresponding global free or vector-bundle presentation hypotheses. The universal quotient is flat over its representing base, not an assertion that that base is flat over S.
hypotheses: Projective/very ample data are fixed; polynomial may give the empty scheme.
Use local free presentations on affine base opens and glue by the represented functor.
proofSteps: The bounded Grassmannian map and flattening give locally closed representability on base opens, compatible on overlaps.

Over a DVR R with fraction field K, extend q_K by the image of E_R→j_*F_K. It is coherent as a quotient of E_R, R-torsion-free and therefore R-flat; its support is proper and its special polynomial equals P. Any flat extension has the same saturated kernel, proving uniqueness.

The valuative criterion gives properness. Choose one sufficiently large m over the finite affine base cover. The canonical map from π_*E(m) to the universal twisted pushforward gives a global map to R09.1/coherent-grassmannian of rank P(m) quotients of the coherent sheaf π_*E(m); the local evaluation reconstruction proves it is an immersion. Properness makes it closed. R09.1/plucker then embeds it in P(∧^{P(m)}π_*E(m)), a coherent projective bundle. This is a global ambient sheaf, not an inference of a global free presentation from local ones. If no nonempty-base family exists, use the empty scheme directly. Nitsure 5.2–5.3 supply the stronger presentation variants.
The all-test-scheme statement follows from the representable construction plus quotient limit preservation, rather than extrapolating an argument restricted to locally Noetherian tests.

nodes.title: The Quot scheme and its universal quotient
nodes.statement: Choose the representing S-scheme Q for fixed-polynomial Quot, with the natural Yoneda identification and the universal quotient on X_Q corresponding to id_Q. Every T→Q pulls this quotient to the corresponding family, uniquely up to its source-commuting isomorphism. The sheaf in the universal quotient is Q-flat, finitely presented with proper support and polynomial P. For every S′→S, Q×_S S′ represents the pulled data, hence is canonically isomorphic to the Quot scheme of those data whenever that chosen model is available; this identification obeys identity and composition coherence.
hypotheses: Noetherian S and the projective hypotheses of quot-projectivity; arbitrary S′ and T are allowed in the represented functor.
Base-change representation remains meaningful without assuming S′ Noetherian.

nodes.title: The universal isomorphism locus of a proper family map
nodes.statement: Let X,Y be proper flat finitely presented over S and let u:X→Y be an S-morphism. There is an open U⊆S such that for every T→S, u_T is an isomorphism if and only if T→S factors through U. In the graph application both the universal closed family and X_H are proper flat finitely presented over H. Consequently the first-projection isomorphism locus is scheme-theoretically universal, including infinitesimal tests.
hypotheses: No conclusion from merely bijective geometric points is substituted for being an isomorphism.

Nitsure 6.5 is the Noetherian, projective-map case. The stated proper finitely presented scheme version is proved by the finite-algebra argument below; Stacks 99.12.2 and its input 76.49.6 (05XD) independently confirm the general universal locus.
proofSteps: Work first over a Noetherian affine base. The map u is proper because its source is proper and its target separated over S. At a fibre where u_s is an isomorphism it is quasi-finite. Remove the proper image in S of the closed complement of its quasi-finite locus. On the resulting neighbourhood u is proper quasi-finite, hence finite, using the two cited Mathlib results.

For finite u, inspect the algebra map O_Y→u_*O_X. Its coherent cokernel vanishes on the isomorphic fibre; Nakayama and properness of Y/S allow removal of the image of its support. After this removal the map is surjective. Both O_Y and u_*O_X are flat over S (for the latter use finite affine pushforward and flatness of X/S). Therefore the short exact kernel sequence stays exact on the fibre. Its coherent kernel also has zero fibre, so the same support/Nakayama argument removes it. The finite algebra map is then an isomorphism, hence so is u.

The union of these neighbourhoods is the open set of fibre isomorphisms. A base-changed isomorphism forces every residue-field fibre to be an isomorphism, since isomorphisms descend under field extensions; conversely a map into this open pulls back the isomorphism already present there. This proves universality on infinitesimal and arbitrary test schemes, not only on geometric points.

For arbitrary S, work affine locally and descend the two proper flat finitely presented families and their map to a Noetherian finite-presentation model using SF.0/finite-presentation-limits. Pull its universal open locus back to S; the universal property makes the constructions agree on overlaps.

nodes.title: Projective Chow test sheaves for dévissage
nodes.statement: For a proper finite-type scheme X over a field k and each integral closed i:Z→X, choose a projective Chow modification g:Y→Z, isomorphic over a dense open of Z. A sufficiently high twist of a very ample O_Y(1) gives G=i_*g_*O_Y(n), coherent with support Z, generic stalk κ(η) and R^qg_*O_Y(n)=0 for q>0. Thus this choice gives generic rank one. A more general proper projective domination gives a nonzero finite-dimensional generic stalk, whose rank may be larger; an exact two-out-of-three class also closed under direct summands and containing these more general witnesses contains every coherent sheaf by coherent-devissage. These are algebraic inputs to the proper cohomological GAGA reduction.
hypotheses: X proper finite type over k; Z integral and closed; n sufficiently large for the chosen g, not a uniform n for every cover.
The analytic comparison and analytic pushforward are supplied by ComplexComparisonPartII:C3, and are not prerequisites of this algebraic theorem.
proofSteps: Use ChowModification for the integral proper Z and its projective Y; choose a relatively very ample sheaf on Y.

Relative Serre vanishing from R09.1/relative-serre kills higher direct images for high twists. Over the Chow isomorphism open, g_*O_Y(n) is invertible, so its stalk at η has residue-field rank one. For a general proper projective domination, high-twist generation on the nonempty generic fibre instead gives positive finite rank.
Proper pushforward preserves coherence and the generic point is on the full support; apply the direct-summand dévissage criterion.

nodes.title: The support of the Chow adjunction defect
nodes.statement: For a proper modification π:X′→X of Noetherian schemes that is an isomorphism over U, and a coherent F on X, the native adjunction unit F→π_*π*F has coherent kernel and cokernel supported on D=X∖U. They are annihilated by a power of an ideal defining D and can be treated on finite closed thickenings via support-power-filtration. This does not assert descent of every coherent sheaf along π, nor vanishing of higher direct images. In the proper-GAGA essential-surjectivity proof this is the algebraic support mechanism; the analytic unit, its coherence, proper comparison, full faithfulness and Ext¹ lifting remain separate C3 inputs.
hypotheses: π proper finite type between Noetherian schemes; F coherent; no flatness of π required.
A fixed native quasi-coherent ideal defining D is available.
proofSteps: Coherent pullback and proper coherent pushforward keep the unit in the coherent category.
Restrict to U and identify the unit with the identity through the open isomorphism; restriction is exact, so its kernel and cokernel restrict to zero.
Apply the ideal-power support lemma, keeping nilpotent thickenings; C3 then uses its own analytic and extension-comparison results.
